#4361. BMW Just Started Making EV Batteries In America. The New iX5 Will Be First In Line

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BMW’s first high-voltage battery factory for electric vehicles in the United States is now up and running in Woodruff, South Carolina. The facility, which is located just 15 miles from the automaker’s car factory in Spartanburg, will supply finished battery packs for no fewer than six Neue Klasse EVs assembled in the U.S., starting with the new iX5 SUV.

According to BMW, the new facility doesn’t build cells from scratch. Instead, it sources ready-made cells from local suppliers, which are then checked at the plant under a “zero-defect” policy. BMW is currently sourcing Gen6 cylindrical cells from AESC in China, but that will change toward the end of the decade, when LG Energy Solution will become the U.S. supplier, while Samsung SDI will supply European factories.

BMW EV battery factory in Woodruff, South Carolina

After analyzing each incoming cell for voltage and other parameters, the factory starts the clustering process, where the battery cells are connected to coolers to ensure optimal insulation and cooling. While the packs go down the assembly line, they are continuously monitored in real time to make sure that each pack goes out the door in tip-top condition.

The company’s latest EV batteries are built using the “cell-to-pack” technique, where cells are no longer arranged in modules. Instead, they’re put directly into the pack enclosure, where they’re protected by a hardened foam. This way, more cells can fit into the same volume, leading to more energy density and more driving range.

In South Carolina, all production staff go through a virtual reality training program, so they can practice real manufacturing operations under realistic conditions before they set foot on the assembly line. What’s more, BMW is relying heavily on artificial intelligence-powered digital assistants and more than 250 robots to output zero-defect batteries. Over 300 employees are currently working at the company’s new battery-making facility.

The Woodruff plant is BMW’s fourth site in its Gen6 battery production network to start series production, after the facilities in Debrecen, Hungary, Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Germany, Shenyang, China, and San Luis Potosí, Mexico.

It took the automaker roughly three years to go from groundbreaking to mass production in South Carolina. Construction of the Woodruff plant began in September 2023, and just one year later, in September 2024, the first manufacturing equipment was installed. In summer 2025, the first pre-series batteries rolled off the assembly line.

What makes the new facility special, besides being BMW’s first battery plant in the U.S., is that during normal operation, it doesn’t use any fossil fuels, with the site’s industrial trucks being powered by hydrogen. As for the latest Gen6 cylindrical cells, they’re touted as having 28% fewer carbon dioxide emissions compared to the cells used in the outgoing iX SUV.

Aston Martin’s two-time F1 champion driver Fernando Alonso will pilot one of the Dreadnoughts, with nine-time World Rally champion Sébastien Loeb and World Rally Raid champion Lucas Mores operating the other two vehicles.

“Aston Martin Dreadnought was conceived to dominate any terrain, under the most extreme circumstances, and come through it all to deliver on its mission. #4358. Tesla Model 3 Maintenance Guide: What Needs Servicing And What Doesn't

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Everybody knows that electric cars are pretty easy on the owner’s wallet when it comes to regular maintenance. They may cost more to buy new than a comparable gas car, but as the miles pile on, there’s no need to worry about engine oil changes and emissions checks. Plus, cheap EVs are already here, with more to come in the near future.

While all of this is true, EVs aren’t exactly maintenance-free. There are still some things that need to be done to keep an electric car running like new for many years after it rolled off the assembly line.

There might not be an engine under the hood, and no manual or automatic transmission to worry about, but EVs still have transmissions, believe it or not. They also have brake fluid, brake pads, and coolant. And all of these—plus others—need attention over the course of a car’s life.

ERANGE EV tires are purpose-built for electric vehicles, combining efficiency, comfort and performance with advanced EcoPoint3 technology.

For this first installment of our new series on EV maintenance, I’ll focus on the Tesla Model 3, one of the best-selling electric models of all time, and a regular occurrence on roads everywhere in the United States, Europe, and beyond.

I’ll go through what maintenance is required by Tesla to keep the warranty intact, and also discuss items that are not part of the company’s service schedule but might still be worth considering for the long run.

The following list may seem a little too simple for someone who has switched from a gas or diesel car to an EV, but there’s no shortage of high-mileage electric cars out there, including countless Teslas, that are still going strong with minimal maintenance. Here’s what Tesla recommends owners look out for on the Model 3:

High-Efficiency Particulate (HEPA) filter and carbon filter replacement: every three years, for vehicles that have them from the factory

Similar to a combustion vehicle, the Tesla Model 3 uses brake fluid to push the brake pads onto the rotors. Brake fluid is hygroscopic, meaning it naturally absorbs moisture from the air. If there’s a lot of moisture contamination, hydraulic pressure drops, which leads to a softer brake pedal and longer braking distances. A brake fluid test reveals if it’s still good or if it needs replacing.

Even though all modern EVs use their electric motors to slow down, they still rely on mechanical brakes to increase safety, and the Model 3 is no different. To keep things running smoothly, Tesla recommends cleaning and lubricating the brake calipers, especially for cars that live in areas where the roads are salted during the winter.

The thickness of the brake pads also needs to be checked, though there have been plenty of cases out there of Tesla EVs with over 100,000 miles on the clock and the original brake pads still in good condition.

Yes, the Model 3 doesn’t have a hot engine, but it still needs a radiator to keep the thermal system running cool. Depending on where the car is located, debris can build up over time, reducing the radiator’s efficiency and limiting the car’s performance.

Tesla Model 3 windshield camera precision cleaning

Tesla’s advanced driver assistance systems rely on video cameras to react, but they can’t perform as intended if they’re obstructed. The company says that cleaning the inside of the windshield in the camera area is vital for clear visibility and optimal camera function.

To check if cleaning is required, owners can tap the Maintenance tab in the infotainment system.

EVs are known for being harder on tires than gas cars because acceleration and brake regeneration will put stress on the rubber. To prolong the life of a tire set, Tesla recommends rotating the tires every 6,250 miles.

This is also when you want to check the tires themselves. Because EVs often wear out tires quicker, it's important to keep an eye on tread depth. When it gets below 4/32nds of an inch, it's time to start looking for new tires. If your tread depth is below 2/32nds, replace them immediately.

If the driver notices vibrations in the steering wheel while driving, the wheels may need balancing. With unbalanced tires, handling, tire life, and steering components are affected.

If the vehicle pulls to one side when the steering wheel is straight, or if there’s uneven wear on the tires, a wheel alignment may be needed. The procedure is also recommended after installing new tires.

All of the vehicle’s maintenance needs can be viewed in the Maintenance Summary on the central touchscreen, which provides a record of when common actions were last performed and recommends when to perform them next.

Tesla says that all of these items need to be performed at an authorized service center. This includes servicing the low-voltage and high-voltage batteries. However, there are some maintenance actions that should be considered by owners who want to treat their EVs as their forever cars.

We’ve all heard of “lifetime fluids,” but ask any well-versed mechanic out there, and they’ll say that they don’t exist. Instead, car manufacturers refer to them when it’s their job to maintain the car under warranty. After the warranty expires, the owner is on the hook for all repairs, including those that could have been avoided.

The following recommendations are nowhere to be found in Tesla’s maintenance plan, but some technicians still recommend them. Even though they’re not required actions, Tesla has service procedures for all of them, and its service centers can perform them if the owner asks.

Tesla used to recommend changing the transmission fluid in its drive units every 100,000 miles, but that went the way of the dodo. Now, the company’s transmissions, which transfer power from the electric motor to the wheels, have built-in filters, but plenty of mechanics out there believe that it’s good practice to renew the fluid every 100,000 miles at the latest.

The Model 3 uses coolant to keep the high-voltage battery at an optimal temperature. Just like on a combustion car, the coolant needs to be checked and replaced if it becomes contaminated.

Over time, rubber bushes will lose their elasticity or even crack. If this happens, knocks or rattles will make their presence felt, requiring a visit to a service center. Even though Tesla implemented many manufacturing novelties over time, it still hasn’t figured out how to replace the age-old rubber bushes found in all cars.

Under warranty, Tesla's authorized service centers should handle all maintenance items. However, after the warranty expires, many of the maintenance actions found on this list can be easily done at home by the owner. Air filter changes and radiator cleaning are DIY jobs that shouldn't take hours to complete, even for people who haven't done any mechanical work before.

Best of all, though, Tesla has published all of its service manuals online, and anyone can follow the service procedures to do maintenance jobs. What's more, in recent years, plenty of independent EV shops have popped up, and they can usually handle repairs and maintenance at lower costs than Tesla. That said, Tesla's own shops will happily inspect and repair older models, too.

Keeping an EV on the road should be much cheaper than a gas car, but it still requires some maintenance. Over a five-year period, the main maintenance items should include at least one set of new tires, multiple tire rotations, two brake fluid tests and maybe one flush, two cabin air filter replacements, several brake checks, and at least one set of wiper blades.

#4355. Tesla Keeps Killing Cars. Now It Wants To Build Cybercabs In Germany

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Tesla’s core lineup is shrinking as the company focuses in on robotaxis. Now, Tesla boss Elon Musk wants to take his autonomous vehicle manufacturing ambitions beyond Texas and begin Cybercab production in Germany.

The company plans to invest €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its factory near Berlin, targeting production of up to one million Cybercabs. According to Reuters, Tesla intends to apply for permits before the end of the year, begin construction in the first half of 2027, and start German Cybercab production in 2029.

The news comes as Tesla keeps reducing the number of conventional cars on offer. Over the past year or so, it has retired entire models, dropped cheaper variants, and earmarked factory space for robots and robotaxis. Knowing that, the new German Cybercab plan starts to look less like an addition to Tesla’s business and more like a replacement for part of it.

The most significant departures this year were the Model S and Model X. Tesla ended both model lines and announced it would repurpose its former Fremont factory space to build Optimus humanoid robots. Granted, the S and X were aging, low-volume products, but they made Tesla look more like a traditional automaker.

The Cybertruck is next, although its departure has become a moving target. Musk initially announced a mid-2027 shutdown to free Texas factory space for Cybercabs, then extended production through the end of summer to fulfill its order backlog. But it’s still scheduled for retirement.

Not even the ubiquitous Model Y has escaped. Tesla dropped its cheapest all-wheel-drive version earlier this month, less than a year after introducing it. Buyers who want two motors must now stretch to the Premium AWD or just get the base rear-wheel-drive variant, which remains available.

Tesla isn’t abandoning human-driven cars altogether. The redesigned Roadster revealed last month is now promised for 2028, complete with thruster-assisted theatrics. After years of delays and a complete redesign, it’s still a vehicle Tesla promises to build.

Basically, the new Roadster offers spectacle, but it doesn’t fill the practical gaps left by a luxury sedan, a large SUV, and a pickup. Tesla doesn’t even seem to be interested in filling those gaps.

The Cybercab faces a different issue. Without manual controls, its usefulness depends on Tesla’s autonomous driving capabilities and permission to deploy them. In the U.S., regulators have already opened an investigation into how the vehicle complies with federal safety requirements. A German production facility doesn’t, by itself, settle where its output can operate.

Tesla’s struggle to get FSD approved in Europe shows how slow that process can be. Dutch regulators cleared the supervised system in April after more than 18 months of testing, but its rollout has since depended on individual countries granting permission. EU-wide approval remains pending, and Tesla has renamed it “Tesla Assisted Driving” and tightened its speed settings to address regulators’ concerns.

All that work is for software that still requires an attentive driver. Getting permission for a Cybercab with no steering wheel or pedals is a separate challenge. And now Tesla wants to build those in Europe…

Still, Tesla’s survival doesn’t only rest on the Cybercab. The Model 3 and Model Y are still very popular worldwide, and the Semi could give it a foothold in electric trucking. But shrinking its passenger car lineup while spending billions on robotaxis leaves Tesla with fewer alternatives if Musk’s driverless future takes longer or proves less profitable than he expects.

Jaguar Land Rover CEO P.B. Balaji confirmed the electric Defender model during a November 13 call, according to Automotive News. JLR executives reportedly confirmed that the Defender EV would be built in Halewood, England, alongside its Range Rover GT sibling. (Road & Track has reached out to JLR for confirmation, and will update the story if we learn more.)

Preliminary figures indicate the Defender EV will likely have less than 450 miles of range, according to Automotive News; the Defender EV will share a battery pack with the Range Rover GT that is estimated for that lofty max range, but its boxy shape will likely prevent it from reaching the same efficiency figures. JLR has yet to reveal official battery capacity for either model.

Hybrid versions of the Defender EV and Range Rover GT are also in the works for the U.S. market, according to the report, as well as other markets where EV adoption has lagged others. However, Balaji reportedly said the hybrid versions of the Defender EV and Range Rover GT would not arrive in 2027. “The project is fully underway, but we won’t catch next year’s timelines,” Balaji said to Automotive News.

#4353. 2028 Scion Kei-01 First Drive: Mite Makes Right

We spent a little bit of time driving a short distance in a tiny pickup that’ll be sold in small numbers.

We haven’t timed one, but eyeballing it, the Scion Kei-01 should reach its top speed before the 1250-hp Chevy Corvette ZR1X reaches 100 mph. (You’re welcome, Toyota marketing team.) Of course, that’s because America’s newest and cutest truck is limited to just 25 mph, per the feds’ FMVSS No. 500 regulation that allows the Kei-01 to be sold here. Toyota is assembling and selling these rebadged Daihatsu Hijets in the United States starting next year, and we got to take one for a short drive—which will be most drives in a pickup this small—to see whether it lives up to the hype.

First, we had to fight our instinct to get into the driver’s seat from the left side. The Kei-01 is right-hand drive, like the Hijet sold in Japan, because Toyota wanted to bring it to the United States as quickly and inexpensively as possible. Production models will get a different backup camera to meet federal requirements, but beyond that, the U.S. version is largely unchanged from the Daihatsu sold in Japan.

See all results for new 2028 Toyota Scion KEI-01 for sale near 94043

Every Kei-01 sold here, mainly to fleets, will have an extended cab, which affords extra cargo space for a shotgun or your largest bushel of chewing tobacco. Or both. The fixed steering column doesn’t tilt or telescope, but stovepipe-hat enthusiasts—and it’s been a while since they’ve heard this—have reason to celebrate, as the one thing this truck does big is headroom.

The Kei-01’s “jumbo” cab is why it stands just 2.9 inches lower in height than an F-150, but it’s a lot easier to get into. You barely have to lift a foot to climb in. A portion of the footwell is painted metal, and your feet are ahead of the front wheel wells. The front axle is practically beneath your butt.

Unlike the workaday pickups you can rent from Home Depot and Menards, this truck, with its massive screen and power windows, is an ergonomic miracle compared with single-cab full-size rentals. Remember when steering wheels were only responsible for turning left and right and occasionally honking the horn? The Kei-01’s wheel is like that. Except the horn’s high-pitched beep is too humiliating to use in anger.

Your fingertips on the steering wheel are so close to the front of the vehicle that they could almost be the hood ornament. Which is certainly novel and makes it super easy to nose in close to objects. Though the lack of a crumple zone aft of your knuckles is a concern that flashes through your mind.

Around the little dirt loop, the Kei-01 offers a driving feel that’s akin to a riding lawn mower. The steering takes nearly 4.5 turns lock-to-lock, but the Kei-01 is still stupid-easy to maneuver. There’s a rawness about scooting around in it that makes you feel like you’re getting paid hourly. This workhorse may be at a speed disadvantage compared to most of the electric scooters in our Gear Team’s roundup, but try hauling hay with one of those.

See all results for new 2028 Toyota Scion KEI-01 for sale near 94043

Underneath all that adorable sheetmetal is a 660-cc three-cylinder engine that sounds about as smooth as a Honda Grom. It’s paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission. Despite its goofy proportions, the Kei-01 isn’t as front-heavy as it looks. With the engine mounted near the middle of the truck, this little box on wheels feels balanced. It lacks a dedicated transfer case, but its four-wheel-drive system has an electronic lock mode to add a bit more confidence on hill climbs.

The best part might be the roughly five-and-a-half-foot bed. Its low load floor makes for a perfect bench, and all three bedsides fold down. Lower the tailgate, or either side, or all three. It’s brilliantly simple and quick. There’s no tall bedside to reach over, and you don’t have to climb into the bed to reach stuff. The truck can handle 600 pounds of cargo too. Seriously, why can’t full-size pickup beds offer this kind of flexibility?

We spent only a short time driving the little Kei-01, but even limited to 25 mph, it’s still rather compelling. And, unlike the used kei trucks imported from Japan, the Scion has a factory warranty. The big unknown still hanging over this small truck is the price, which Toyota hasn’t announced yet. When all you need is a little truck, without most of the drawbacks of a big one, the Kei-01 certainly fits.

#4352. Mercedes Is Bringing Hands-Free Driving To Certain U.S. Highways In 2027

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Mercedes is bringing a new suite of driver assistance features. The two big new ones are Mercedes' MB.Drive Assist Pro, an FSD-like system we recently tested, and Hands-Free Highway Assist.

Silly corporate naming conventions aside, this new system is impressive. MB.Drive Assist Pro is a true point-to-point system, capable of taking you from your starting point to your destination on its own in urban environments as long as you directly supervise it. Mercedes is still calling it an SAE Level 2 system, so you still need to pay attention, keep your hands on the wheel, and take over whenever it needs. But it can do the heavy lifting for you.

On the highway, the Hands-Free Highway Assist can completely take over inputs on approved roads at speeds up to 85 mph. You'll need radar cruise engaged to use it. Once it's on, though, it can change lanes, overtake slower vehicles, handle lane merging, and even take off-ramps for you on its own, assuming the conditions are appropriate. Think of it like Super Cruise, just from Mercedes.

"By bringing hands-free highway driving together with point-to-point assistance and expanding these technologies across our portfolio, we’re making them available to more customers across the U.S.," said Jason Hoff, CEO Mercedes-Benz North America. "That’s where sophisticated technology becomes meaningful: when it makes everyday driving more comfortable and convenient.”

China has already had the system, but Mercedes is going to begin bringing it to German and the U.S. The latter of which will actually get a sneak preview of it in December, 2026, but only in California. Select Californian customers will be able to participate in an Early Access Program (EAP), which will let them test out these new features. Only lessees of the 2026/2027 Mercedes CLA, 2027 GLC Electric SUV2, S-Class Sedan, GLE SUV and Coupe, and GLS will be eligible.

Rollout for the rest of the country will happen in Spring 2027, and it will be available for all Mercedes vehicles with the proper hardware equipped. Even owners of existing vehicles with the necessary hardware will be able to buy the feature and have it digitally installed via an over-the-air update.

#4351. International Auto Theft Ring Busted in Canada, Cops Say, 96 Stolen Vehicles Worth $3 Million Recovered En Route to Africa

Luxury SUVs and sedans were among the vehicles recovered during a Canadian investigation targeting an alleged theft network.

Police in Canada say they have busted an organized auto theft crime ring that was stealing cars from the Great White North and shipping them across the ocean to Africa. Authorities announced a total of over 200 charges against 12 arrested individuals associated with the crime. In addition, officers recovered more than 90 vehicles worth a combined $4.5 million Canadian—$3.15 million in U.S. dollars.

While the charges and announcement came on Monday, authorities have been putting this case together since March, when officers of the Peel Regional Police in Ontario put together what they called “Project Cadetta” in partnership with the Canada Border Services Agency. Together, they initially focused on a single warehouse in Brampton, which allegedly was the staging area for stolen cars that were destined for West Africa via Canadian shipping ports. As police investigated the space, they began linking individuals to other locations.

Authorities say that many of these cars would get different VIN numbers as a part of the scheme. While they didn't detail the vehicles in question, they did show photos of a few; among them are several Lexus vehicles, a Land Rover Range Rover Sport, a Toyota Land Cruiser, and a BMW XM.

If this sounds familar, it’s not just you; this year alone, we at Road & Track have reported on similar theft rings several times. In April, authorities in the U.S. charged six people with being part of an illegal operation to steal cars and ship them to Africa. Police linked the suspects to some 130 cars. Then, later in the same month, police in New York said they found 72 more cars destined for West Africa. The cars in question included a Rolls-Royce, several BMWs, and an Audi SQ8. In May, Canadian police found another 40 stolen cars involved with a similar theft ring.

#4350. 2026 Toyota GRMN Corolla First Drive: A Blur of Nür

Toyota’s most expensive Corolla ever bristles with track-focused hardware.

Slapping Turn 1’s bright-green curbing, it’s immediately clear that the GR team has done something really good. I’m driving the Toyota GRMN Corolla at Eagles Canyon Raceway in Texas, and the first 30 seconds of recorded voice notes are just me eagerly repeating “Aw, yeah” at various parts of the track.

The GRMN, which stands for “Gazoo Racing tuned by Meister of Nürburgring,” receives an incredible amount of attention for a car Toyota won’t build more than 730 of. The changes are as juicy as workplace gossip. Ten slots are cut into the underside of the carbon-fiber hood to direct air where Toyota says it will contribute to more predictable steering at high speeds. Engineers shortened the front suspension’s bump-stop stroke by four millimeters while adding two millimeters at the rear, helping the car settle over curbing. There’s also a taller first gear and a pinch more torque in the midrange. And finally, an optional oil cooler keeps the all-wheel-drive system happy.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota GR Corolla for sale near 02903

Toyota’s obsession over details is admirable. The GRMN’s improvements over the standard GR Corolla are so subtle that they may go unnoticed by most folks and even some car nerds. I started my track time with an automatic GR Corolla, then switched to the GRMN and back. While the car looks only slightly different, the driving experience is wildly new.

The steering is the first major giveaway. Immediately, the GRMN feels much tighter and more direct in turns than the regular GR Corolla. Turn-in is dramatically quicker, and return to center is noticeably stronger. Initially, I thought Toyota had maybe beefed up its steering-rack slider. Nope. It’s largely the same hardware, but with an aggressive electric power-steering calibration. Adding to the different steering feel is a thinner steering-wheel rim, because even if it saved GR engineers less than an ounce, it still counts.

But it’s the suspension that really shines here. Eagles Canyon is rife with elevation changes, including several corners with curbing that would upset the automatic GR and send it bouncing upon landing. But like a honey badger, the GRMN don’t care. There’s no ugly secondary motion; you certainly feel the curb, but the nose stays flat on impact. Toyota developed special monotube dampers with internal rebound springs to help maintain tire contact, while its bump-stop changes convince you corner exit speeds are higher than ever. It’s the most Porsche-like behavior I’ve experienced in any car that competes with a Hyundai Elantra.

It’s worth noting that the regular GR that I drove wore Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tires, while the GRMN was on much stickier Pilot Sport Cup 2s. Some of the additional grip and steering response is absolutely down to the rubber, but the way the suspension manages impacts and keeps the body under control is an improvement that can’t be credited to tires alone.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota GR Corolla for sale near 02903

There is one exception to the GRMN’s good times that not even GRMN chief engineer Naoyuki Sakamoto could explain. During quick countersteering inputs, the electric steering occasionally delivers an unnatural kick through the wheel. It feels as though the power assist has reached its limit, though just for a moment. We experienced it three times over at least 20 laps, but never during our street drive.

The GRMN uses that same ole G16E-GTS 300-hp turbocharged 1.6-liter three-cylinder. Torque increases by just seven pound-feet to 302, with Toyota concentrating the additional grunt between 4000 and 4600 rpm, where the engine spent much of its time at Eagles Canyon clawing out of corners.

The six-speed manual gets its own collection of changes. The close-ratio EA68F gearbox has a taller first gear and a shorter third gear, changing how the engine works through its powerband. Engineers even revised the shifter-cable mount to make the action more direct. Having driven a manual GR recently, the difference is obvious. It’s not Honda Civic Type R good, but it’s still really good.

The GRMN also has additional cooling hardware and a driver-actuated intercooler water-spray system. The only other car I’ve ever driven with one of these was the Subaru WRX STI S209, which would make for a rather interesting comparison test if Subaru still built it. A one-gallon water tank sits beneath the GRMN’s cargo floor, supplying enough water to spray the intercooler for approximately 150 seconds. Toyota claims this can lower intake temperatures by roughly 14 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit. Unfortunately, it’s somewhat difficult to see the status of the system, as there’s no indication in the gauge cluster. Instead, the small button has an even tinier amber light that blinks slowly while two nozzles spray water onto the intercooler. It’s no place to have your eyes pointed while setting lap times, and it left us prayin’ it was still sprayin’.

The most important update may be the optional oil cooler for the all-wheel-drive transfer unit. During Lightning Lap testing in regular GR Corollas at Virginia International Raceway, we’ve experienced overheating that triggers the dreaded “AWD System Overheated” warning. Toyota’s solution circulates gear oil through a separate heat exchanger using an electric pump, roughly doubling the system’s oil capacity in the process.

However, the cooler isn’t standard equipment, and installing it involves more than bolting on a few hoses. It requires an ECU reflash and activation procedure, as the system’s electrical demands also introduce a fuel-economy penalty. Toyota installed the accessory on our GRMN before we took it onto the circuit. Its own testing suggests the system will prevent the AWD system from ever entering 2WD mode. That’s promising, although even 20 laps at Eagles Canyon (with the front straight closed) aren’t enough to declare the problem solved. We’d love to see how it handles VIR’s 4.1-mile Grand Course.

Eventually, Toyota representatives politely suggested I take a break from lapping the GRMN, motioning toward the line of other journalists in the pits. Ugh, fine. Later, I got another turn behind the wheel for the drive from the track to the hotel. And what a completely different experience that was.

As in the GR Corolla Morizo Edition, Toyota has stripped the rear seats from this four-door hatchback as part of an effort to reduce weight by 66 pounds. The rear windows are fixed. There’s no rear wiper either, which Toyota says saves about two pounds.

The GRMN is incredibly loud on public roads. With the rear seats removed, there’s little separating the cabin from the racket coming from behind. Those Cup 2 tires scream over mixed asphalt, their noise changing pitch with every new section of pavement. On the highway, you find yourself yelling at the passenger next to you, and not because they started talking politics.

The ride is similarly uncompromising. The same suspension that so calmly devours curbing at Eagles Canyon can make ordinary pavement feel jarring. Even the steering, which I couldn’t stop praising on the circuit, takes some getting used to, as it’s so quick on the street, where small inputs produce immediate responses.

I guess that’s why they didn’t name it the Corolla GR Route 380.

The GRMN Corolla starts at $65,655, which is about $24K more than the standard car. That almost GR86-sized price gap is no small upcharge for a Corolla that’s heavy on track ability and light on everyday ability. It’s also interesting that of the 730 GRMN Corollas being built, none will be sold in Germany, home of the actual Nürburgring; it’s a Japan, Australia, and North America offering only.

At one point during the drive event, one of the GRMNs picked up a nail in its tire, and Toyota had to pull it from the drive rotation to give it fresh Michelins. Rather than sit around and pout (as journalists sometimes do), influencers and editors climbed into the regular automatic GR Corolla for a few laps. The lack of complaining during that inconvenience proves my next point.

The GRMN’s biggest rival is the regular GR Corolla. The new car’s tiny yet important improvements make it considerably better on track, but is a few tenths per lap worth $24K? Not to mention the street-driving inconveniences? Maybe, for some. For everyone else, there’s a perfectly good GR Corolla with rear seats that doesn’t require earplugs.

#4349. The Electric Baby Land Rover Defender And Range Rover GT Will Begin Production Next Year

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

JLR's all-electric baby Defender is coming soon. According to Car and Driver, JLR boss PB Balaji recently said on an earnings call that the smaller, all-electric Defender will go into production at the end next year, alongside the upcoming Range Rover GT. There's no official name for the bite-sized Defender, but Balaji reportedly didn't want to call it the Defender Sport.

While JLR didn't give much info on what the electric baby Defender will be, we do know that it will be built on the same Electrified Modular Architecture (EMA) platform that underpins the Range Rover GT. So it makes sense that it'll be built at the same factory. That factory currently builds the existing piston-powered Discovery Sport and the Range Rover Evoque. So JLR is basically just replacing the current combustion cars with their new electric counterparts.

Despite both cars being built in the same factory, Balaji seemed to suggest that only the Defender will go into production in 2027. There's not much word on any technical specs just yet, but EMA supports 800-volt architectures and is capable of housing both pure battery-electric powertrains and hybrids. The baby Defender could very well offer both, but whichever powertrain it has, it'll need to be capable off-road to deliver on its name.

According to Motor1, Mark Cameron, managing director of Defender and Discovery brands, said "We have got to make sure everything we do as Defender has the DNA of the brand: epic built-to-last, go-anywhere capability."

Pricing, specs, and range are all still under wraps, although it might make sense for either new electric product to have the same 118.5-kWh battery as the current Range Rover Electric. With it, the electric Rover is capable of 333 miles of range, and that uses a conventional platform. The battery is also capable of 350 kW DC fast-charging, which would be very competitive in the segment, so it might make sense for JLR to roll with that battery tech. The big Range Rover Electric has a dual-motor powertrain, with 542 horsepower, but that might be a bit much for a baby Defender. Although, there could be a go-fast version with that much power, similar to the current Defender Octa.

Land Rover pushed the current full-size Defender's electric replacement out to sometime in the 2030s, so there shouldn't be any confusion between the full-size and bite-size models. If production begins in late 2027, that means we could see the baby Defender soon.

#4348. The Ford Mustang GTD 1901 Takes Inspiration From a 125-Year-Old Race Car

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

The Blue Oval is celebrating a century and a quarter of racing history with a special-edition Mustang GTD.

Henry Ford was racing cars before the Mustang, GT40, or even the Ford Motor Company itself existed. Back in 1901, he won his first race behind the wheel of a two-cylinder race car nicknamed “Sweepstakes,” a car that produced just 26 horsepower. 125 years later, Ford has unveiled the 815-horsepower 2028 Mustang GTD 1901—a special edition inspired by the car that helped launch Henry Ford's automotive empire.

The Mustang GTD 1901 has a 789-horsepower advantage over the Sweepstakes car, but the design inspiration is clear. The Mustang GTD 1901 features a distinctive Royal Red exterior and a wide, off-center black racing stripe featuring a bright red centerline. The color combination reverses the original race car's black body and deep red chassis components. Additional diagonal graphics and exposed carbon-fiber elements, including the front splitter, rocker panels, rear diffuser, and wing, complete the exterior look.

Have a seat inside the Mustang GTD 1901, and you immediately realize this is not an ordinary GTD—that is, if there is even such a thing as an ordinary GTD. The first thing you notice are the Mahogany Red leather seats with Race Red stitching. Keep looking, and you’ll see there are also matching red accents on the seatbelts, while the steering wheel receives Mahogany Red faux suede.

The Performance Package is standard equipment on the Mustang GTD 1901. Options include the magnesium wheels, which reduce the unsprung weight by 50.3 pounds. If you want to spice up the interior, you can order the optional titanium trim package, which gets you redesigned titanium shifter paddles that have been lengthened for the 2028 model year. The titanium trim in the GTD, by the way? It comes from retired F-22 fighter jets.

Ford has not announced how many Mustang GTD 1901’s will be built, or how much they will cost. But we wouldn’t count on seeing too many at your local track day.

A lot has changed since Henry Ford won his first race; horsepower figures, aerodynamics, and suspension technology have come a long way. But the desire of the company that bears his name to prove itself on the racetrack apparently hasn't changed much at all, and that’s something we’re certainly thankful for.

#4346. Bentley’s First EV Is Already Sold Out, And Production Hasn’t Even Started

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Bentley’s first electric car, the Torcal SUV, looks like a hit already. Even though production hasn’t started yet, the $220,000+ EV is sold out for 2027, according to Frank-Steffen Wallier, the company’s head honcho, quoted by Automotive News.

The British luxury automaker said that all available production slots for next year have already been allocated and that the company is now taking orders that will be delivered in 2028. Bentley didn’t say how many EVs it will build in 2027, but the initial customer response has made the marque quite happy with the outcome.

“Needless to say, we’re very pleased with the response and position we’re in,” a company spokesperson told Automotive News.

That’s great news for Bentley, which isn’t doing great in terms of sales and profit. From January through September, it sold 5,970 cars globally, 17% fewer compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, the profit dropped by more than half to $54.1 million through the first nine months of the year.

The Torcal, which is smaller than the Bentayga SUV, is the brand’s cheapest model, though it still costs a pretty penny. The base Torcal starts at $222,495, followed by the more powerful Torcal S at $262,695, and the Torcal First Edition at $300,995. All things considered, Walliser said that the smaller size and relatively lower price compared to the Bentayga have attracted new and younger customers to the brand.

By comparison, the Bentayga starts at $231,150, the Flying Spur sedan starts at $254,850, and the Continental GT two-door starts at $288,750.

So far, the Torcal S has proved to be the most popular version of the new EV, but when it comes to personalization, the sky’s the limit. “We see cars spec’d north of 300,000 pounds ($397,086),” said Walliser. “Individual content does not stop in case of an electric car. There have been some assumptions, and some people have been critical if people would be ready to do so.”

Based on the same underpinnings as the electric Porsche Cayenne, the Bentley Torcal is powered by a 113-kilowatt-hour battery that can be charged at up to 400 kilowatts. It can go from 10% to 80% in less than 20 minutes, and the estimated EPA range is expected to be over 300 miles.

Built on the Premium Platform Electric (PPE) architecture, it has two electric motors that make 810 horsepower and 881 pound-feet of torque in the standard Torcal and a whopping 876 hp and 996 lb-ft of torque in the Torcal S. When the model debuted in September, Bentley said it was the most powerful and quietest model to come out of the factory in Crewe.

To make the Torcal a reality, Bentley invested $463 million to upgrade its factory in England, plus at least the same amount for supply chain preparations and research and development, Walliser said.

Despite the electric SUV’s initial success, the British automaker is still heavily invested in gas and plug-in hybrid models, and the Bentayga isn’t going anywhere. “We have a very good combination with Torcal and Bentayga,” Walliser said. “The segment definitely has space for two cars.”

#4345. The Ford Maverick’s New SV300T Package Makes It a Legit Street Truck

A Mustang-sourced turbocharger helps push the little pickup’s output to 300 hp, and the lowered versions adopt a unique look.

Street trucks, real ones, are more than a flashy appearance package. Thankfully, Ford is committed to legit performance, as we can see with the new SV300T package developed by Ford Custom Garage for the Maverick pickup truck. Sure, the kit includes some prominent styling changes, like black or bronze body graphics and matching 20-by-8-inch wheels, but it also makes the engine more powerful and upgrades the chassis to be more playful.

The SV300T treatment is available on 2025–2026 Maverick XLT, Lariat, and Lobo models, with the former two requiring the turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder and all-wheel-drive system that’s standard on the Lobo. That setup is normally good for 250 horsepower and 280 pound-feet of torque, but those figures rise to 300 horses and 350 pound-feet. That’s attributed to the Maverick adopting a turbocharger from the EcoBoost Mustang that brings a larger compressor wheel (59 versus 53 mm), and it’s paired with a Ford Performance intercooler. Naturally, this setup benefits from a custom calibration. The soundtrack is provided by a Borla exhaust.

See all results for new 2026 Ford Maverick for sale near 94043

Along with more power, the XLT and Lariat versions of the Maverick SV300T receive an upgraded chassis that turns them into true street trucks. The list includes lowering springs, bigger anti-roll bars, and dampers from the Lobo, which already includes these parts as well as larger front brake rotors clamped by two-piston calipers. The latter is optional on the XLT and Lariat versions. If you’re wondering whether Lobo customers get a discount for not needing the extra add-ons, don’t worry, they do.

For those who order the SV300T package directly from Ford, it can be installed on the XLT and Lariat for an extra $15,595; the Lobo version costs $2000 less. For reference, the ‘26 version of the Lobo starts at $37,775, while the turbocharged XLT and Lariat start at $32,490 and $37,715, respectively. You can do the math if you want the totals for the SV300T-equipped Mavericks, which Ford says include installation, recommended tires, and transportation. Everything also comes with a three-year or 36,000-mile warranty.

If you already own an eligible Maverick and prefer to find your own ASE-certified technician to do the install, the price of the SV300T package drops considerably to $4500 for the Lobo and $6075 for the XLT and Lariat.

#4344. Gift Guide: 44 Cool, Fun, and Unique Gifts for Motorcyclists

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

We've tested and compiled an array of motorcycle gifts, gear, and accessories to help you find the right gifts for the motorcycle riders in your life.

This article was updated in November 2026.

The best motorcycle gifts don’t have to be flashy. A well-chosen upgrade can make a cold commute more comfortable, a long tour easier to manage, or time in the garage more rewarding. The trick is matching the present to the person: what they ride, where they go, and what gear they already own.

This guide covers a range of options, from protective apparel and useful electronics to compact accessories and garage staples. Whether you’re shopping for a longtime rider or someone still getting used to life on two wheels, you’ll find ideas for different styles, needs, and budgets.

Kriega is the leading brand in motorcycle baggage, and its backpacks are no different. Waterproof inside and with 20 liters of storage space, the R20 backpack is perfect for commuting and features Kreiga's harness-style fasteners. An innovative technology pioneered specifically for motorcycles, the chest clip and straps allow the bag's weight to be pushed forward, making sure that the weight stays centered on the back without disturbing your riding balance.

It's the perfect motorcycling backpack as far as we're concerned.

Give a motorcyclist a gift that makes every ride easier to relive—and can help document the unexpected. The Insta360 X5 Motorcycle Bundle captures 8K 360-degree video, letting riders choose angles later instead of fiddling with framing on the road. FlowState stabilization smooths bumpy footage, while the heavy-duty clamp and invisible selfie stick are ready for bike-mounted shots. It’s a fun way to share adventures and a useful record if a ride takes an unwelcome turn.

This extremely compact starter box is 33% thinner, 27% smaller, and 34% lighter than most portable jump-packs, so it slips right into your pocket. Rated at 1500 amps, it can even jump-start cars, motorcycles, trucks, ATVs, boats, RVs, vans, and SUVs. Best of all, it's equipped with a flashlight and two fast-charging USB ports, both A and C, so it can easily charge your favorite USB devices while it's in your pocket. No motorcyclist should flip up the kickstand without one.

This helmet wall mount is perfect for those who want to save space. It easily mounts on any wall and swivels to display helmets or other items as desired. When not in use, it can be pushed against the wall to take up less space. A bottom hook lets you hang your jacket, keeping all your riding gear together.

Hand signals from your riding buddy can only go so far, especially when a waving arm could mean anything. Communication systems go a long way toward enjoying group rides and Cardo's PackTalk PRO is the perfect communication system for individual and group use. The waterproof model includes a mesh network Bluetooth connection for phone calls, directions, and music while also allowing for rider-to-rider communications. JBL speakers are included in the package and make communications and music crystal clear. Best of all, you can set up voice commands and speed dial to make sure those eyes stay on the road.

Few gifts can improve a rider's safety as dramatically as the Brake Free Helmet Light. This clever wireless device mounts to the back of nearly any helmet and uses built-in sensors to detect braking, downshifting, and engine braking, illuminating bright LEDs at eye level for drivers behind you. With no wiring, no apps, and a weatherproof design, it's an easy upgrade that boosts visibility day or night. For riders who value safety without sacrificing simplicity, this is one of the smartest gifts on the road.

For the rider who owns the gloves, jacket, and boots, give them something that matters most when a ride goes wrong: Alpinestars’ Tech-Air 5 Plasma airbag system. This lightweight, breathable vest slips beneath a motorcycle jacket and deploys to protect the chest, ribs, back, and shoulders. It offers STREET, OFF-ROAD, and RACE modes, up to 30 hours of battery life, and a user-replaceable inflator. It’s an investment in safer miles—and a thoughtful gift with purpose. Available in sizes XS-4XL.

You don't need to be a biker to love this Lego set. It includes a two-speed gearbox and front and rear suspension for realistic movement. The attention to detail is impressive, like the turning handlebar and front and rear disc brakes. A kickstand, exhaust pipe, windshield, and dashboard add the little details that make this model true to the full-size version. Designed in collaboration with Ducati, it's a Technic set, so it's far more than just a toy or model. Still, Lego enthusiasts who want a bigger challenge should try the 1900-piece Technic BMW M 1000 RR ($249.99 at Lego) set.

Quad Lock makes a huge variety of phone-mounting gear, and motorcyclist-specific products are some of the most popular. This particular unit, the Quad Lock Motorcycle Handlebar Mount, includes everything you'll need to install it on any motorcycle and allows for your choice of mounting angle. You'll also need to get one of QuadLock's sleek phone cases to complete the package.

Some riders don't like to wear big clunky boots. Now they can go straight from the bike to the bar with these comfortable moto-specific riding shoes. Affordable, practical, and useful on nearly every ride, it's a stocking stuffer any motorcyclist will appreciate.

#4343. BYD Is Winning Over Japan With A Very Japanese Kind Of EV

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BYD’s latest milestone in Japan would barely register on its sales charts back home in China. But selling 10,000 cars in a country dominated by domestic brands is progress, especially when part of that momentum comes from selling a vehicle tailored to what Japanese buyers actually want: a small, practical box on wheels, which also happens to be electric.

The Chinese automaker announced that its cumulative Japanese passenger-car sales had passed 10,000. Its first 5,000 took roughly two and a half years after deliveries began in January 2023. The next 5,000 took about 15 months. That includes its entire lineup, rather than just its newest and arguably most interesting addition: the Racco electric kei car.

It was bold to challenge Japan’s homegrown manufacturers with something designed specifically for their market and to create the world’s first kei car from a non-Japanese automaker. The Racco’s tall body, tiny footprint, and sliding rear doors follow the familiar Japanese formula for such vehicles. BYD didn’t need to reinvent anything, but its entry needed to be convincing.

Japanese buyers’ initial response to the Racco was encouraging. Launched on July 28, it attracted 1,002 orders in two weeks, the fastest order intake of any BYD model in Japan. By the end of August, that had grown to around 1,500. Roughly 80% of buyers chose the range-topping 300 Premium, clearly showing that the cheapest version was less attractive.

BYD credited the Racco with helping deliver record monthly orders across its Japanese lineup in August. Potential buyers who came to see the little EV ended up discovering its other models, too.

BYD offers six passenger-car models in Japan, and every one has a charging port. Five are fully electric: the Racco kei car, Dolphin hatchback, Seal sedan, Atto 3 crossover, and Sealion 7 SUV. The sixth, the Sealion 6 SUV, is a plug-in hybrid combining a gasoline engine with electric propulsion. That makes the entire lineup electrified, with no gasoline-only cars or conventional, non-plug-in hybrids on offer.

What’s more interesting is comparing the Racco’s sales performance to its main rival, the Nissan Sakura EV, which is also Japan’s best-selling electric car. In October, the Sakura EV sold 878 units, while the Racco sold 607. That’s almost 70% of the volume, marking a 37% rise over September.

The Nissan Sakura EV was Japan’s electric bestseller for a fourth consecutive year in 2025, but it could lose its crown to the Racco, which gives buyers more battery for less money, at least before subsidies. It starts at ¥2.145 million with a 22.4-kWh pack and 130 miles (210 kilometers) of WLTC range, while the Sakura starts at ¥2.449 million with a 20-kWh battery and 112 miles (180 km).

Even the longer-range Racco, with a 35.8-kWh pack capable of 199 miles (320 km), undercuts the entry-level Nissan at ¥2.398 million. The BYD also gets sliding rear doors instead of the Nissan’s conventional ones. What could help the Sakura stay ahead is the larger government subsidy it benefits from, which can make it cheaper to buy despite its higher sticker price.

It’s a tad early to call the Racco a Japanese sensation, but buyers are clearly interested. This newcomer is already selling roughly seven cars for every ten Sakuras in one month, so it definitely deserves attention.

#4340. Mercedes-Benz Will Sell a C111 Rotary Supercar Prototype for the First Time in History

No copies of the 1970s-era gullwing wedges have ever been available for public ownership before.

There’s no shortage of rare, collectable, crazy-desirable classic Mercedes-Benz vehicles out there for the discerning car collector. Some of the Three-Pointed Star’s cars have gone down in history among the most expensive automobiles ever sold; there’s the $11.8 million 1936 Mercedes-Benz 540 K Special Roadster by Sindelfingen, the $10.2 million 2002 Mercedes-Benz CLK GTR Roadster, and of course, the 1955 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé that sold for over $140 million back in 2022, making it the world’s most valuable car.

But no matter how rich, how connected, how much of a master of the universe you are, you’ve never been able to buy one of Mercedes-Benz’s most ground-breaking machines: the rotary-powered C111. Or at least, that was the case. Come next year, for the very first time, one lucky person will be able to take the Apollo-era wundercar home.

Fans of the brand certainly need no introduction to this wedge-shaped beauty, but for those of you who might not be as current on your Mercedes history, the C111 was revealed at the 1969 International Motor Show (IAA) in Frankfurt, less than two months after Neil Armstrong plopped his boots on the moon. The idea was to create a gullwinged successor to the iconic W198-gen 300SL that dominated racing in the 1950s, packed with then-impressive technology: Wankel rotary engines, fiberglass bodywork, and multi-link rear suspension, all wrapped in a gorgeous period design.

Yet while 17 prototypes were ultimately made, the car never entered production. Rumor has it that interested parties practically channeled Philip J. Fry shouting “Shut up and take my money” by mailing blank checks to the company’s home office, but Mercedes said no dice, citing the Wankel motor’s inability to play nicely with the 1973 oil crisis. (That also kept the motor from winding up in the S-Class, as Mercedes-Benz Classic head of collection Dennis Heck said.) Instead, the copies served as company test beds for years, performing tasks like high-speed testing at Nardo with a variety of different powertrains and aerodynamic kits.

The car in question that will be up for grabs is the third one ever made, a C111-II variant known internally as “Car 33” that comes equipped with its original 2.4-liter 4-rotor engine making 345 horsepower and 289 lb-ft connected to a 5-speed manual gearbox. It was used as part of the Mercedes test fleet, trialing features like anti-lock brakes and a component to empty its twin fuel tanks at even rates—a handy feature in a car capable of 186 miles per hour.

The car was restored to working order two years ago at the Mercedes-Benz Classic Center, although the patina of the Weißherbst-colored exterior and gray-and-white houndstooth patterned interior was kept delightfully intact. As of last month’s photo shoot, its odometer showed 24,766 kilometers—15,355 miles.

The C111 in question will hit the auction block on February 3, 2027, at the Palais du Louvre as part of RM Sotheby’s Retromobile Paris auctions, with the funds raised by the sale used to help the automaker further develop the Mercedes-Benz museum in Stuttgart, including the creation of a digital twin of the museum that will let people access it virtually.

Given its provenance, I would not expect it to go cheap. Neither does the company. “We do believe it will come to a significant double-digit euro [price at auction],” CEO of Mercedes-Benz Heritage GmbH Marcus Breitschwerdt told Road & Track.

“It’s gonna be in excess of twenty-five [million] euros,” RM Sotheby’s president Gord Duff added. “There will be strong activity. It’s one of those things you could never get until now.”

And if you’re thinking, Ehh, they’ve broken the seal on sales, I’ll wait until they auction off another one—well, you’d better be prepared to hold off until 2051 or so, because Mercedes says this sale includes a contractual commitment that it will not sell any more C111s for the next 25 years. Should you be interested in bidding, you can find out more here.

You can often find him test-driving new cars in New York City, cursing the slow-moving traffic surrounding him.

#4339. Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV Owners Can Now Plug And Charge At Electrify America

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The ability to simply plug in at a fast-charging station and start charging within seconds was once a luxury once reserved for Tesla drivers at Superchargers. However, with the advent of Plug & Charge, this seamless operation has come to many other brands, including General Motors. GM announced Plug & Charge support back in 2022, starting with EVGo. Now, Plug & Charge is all in one space via GM's Energy Pass App, with Ionna and ChargePoint added to the Plug & Charge list in 2026. Today, it confirmed support for the largest CCS fast-charging network in the country: Electrify America.

The update comes to CCS-equipped General Motors EVs, with NACS-equipped EVs to follow in early 2027.

To use Plug & Charge with Electrify America (or any other charging network that has a Plug & Charge agreement with GM), the driver must be registered with GM’s Energy Pass in the MyChevrolet, MyGMC, or MyCadillac app. The Energy Pass links your EV with a default payment type, allowing charging stations to start the charging event and bill the driver directly without navigating any other app. The driver doesn’t have to do anything but plug in; there’s no need to use a third-party app or fiddle around with a frustrating interface on the charger itself.

The function works with Ionna, EVGo, and ChargePoint, and now Electrify America. The Energy Pass section of the apps not only controls payment, but serves as a one-stop-shop by showing past charging history and letting you locate and navigate to charging stations.

GM EVs with CCS ports will still have to wait for Plug & Charge support at Tesla Superchargers. But for GM vehicles with NACS ports—including the 2026 Optiq and most 2027 model year cars—can automatically begin charging at Tesla stations.

In order to get more people behind the wheel of EVs, industry leaders have stressed that the ease and quality of charging stops must improve. This goes beyond just making sure there are enough charging stations available and making sure they’re in working order. From start to finish, the charging experience should be easy and painless. Saving time and making things as seamless as possible should help make the charging experience nearly frictionless, which is a good thing for EV adoption.

“Bringing that experience to GM EV drivers is another important step forward. It removes friction from the charging experience and lets customers focus on what matters: plugging in, charging, and getting back on the road.” Robert Barrosa, president and CEO of Electrify America, said in a press release.

GM says that on average, the flow of power should start within 45 seconds of plugging in. That is significantly quicker and easier than navigating through a series of menus and apps to start a charging event without Plug & Charge.

Importantly, the addition of Electrify America brings 6,200 chargers that are capable of speeds of up to 350 kW. Some of GM’s largest EVs, like the Chevrolet Silverado EV or Cadillac Escalade IQ, advertise their charging times when connected these ultra-fast charger.

Participation in GM Energy Pass is optional. If the driver doesn’t want to use it, they are free to use the existing charging station apps to charge the vehicle. But it should be easier to use Energy Pass, at least at Electrify America, EVGo, and Ionna stations.

(Correction 11/18/26 at 10:21 AM ET: This story originally said GM had not rolled out Plug & Charge support for Tesla Superchargers. That is incorrect. GM EVs with native NACS ports already support Plug & Charge at Tesla stations, and CCS vehicles should get the same capability sometime soon.)

#4337. BMW Is Recalling i5 and i7 EVs Over Software Error That Could Lead to an Electric Shock

The automaker is recalling 286 examples of the electric sedans after discovering some received the wrong high-voltage battery software.

A classic BMW 2002 is a simple, mechanical machine. However, a modern BMW sedan is a rolling computer, one that relies heavily on software. And when that software is buggy, issues can arise—which is why the software is tested extensively before going to production. But what happens when that test software mistakenly makes it into production cars?

According to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recall report, BMW is recalling 286 i5 and i7 electric sedans in the United States because some vehicles may have been equipped with testing software, instead of the production software intended to manage high-voltage battery charging. In rare cases, this could expose people to a higher risk of an electric shock.

The recall includes 236 examples of the 2026–2027 BMW i5, including the eDrive40, xDrive40, and M60 variants. Another 50 vehicles are 2027 BMW i7 50 xDrive and 60 xDrive models. All the affected vehicles were manufactured between May and July 2026.

BMW first became aware of the issue on October 8, 2026, when high-voltage battery charging port supplier TE Connectivity Solutions GmbH alerted the automaker. An investigation ensued, and it was discovered that some charging units were mistakenly shipped with test software instead of production software. BMW is not aware of any injuries or accidents related to this problem.

No hardware changes are required to rectify the issue, and the affected vehicles will require a software update. The recall report does not specify that this can be fixed via an over-the-air update, so a trip to the dealer will likely be required.

BMW plans to mail owner notification letters beginning December 25, 2026, although we doubt the U.S.P.S. will be doing much picking up or delivery that day. Starting that same date, owners can also check their vehicle's recall status through the NHTSA recall website by using their VIN, but we suggest waiting until after the kids are done opening presents.

#4336. REO Runabout vs. Slate Truck: Which Sub-$30,000 Truck Is Better?

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Like the idea of a Slate but don't want an EV? Well, an upstart from Dallas, Texas has just the thing for you. That is, if it ever becomes a reality. Startup company REO recently unveiled renderings of its new truck, dubbed the Runabout. It's a similar idea to Slate, with just one basic frame, three different body variants to choose from, no frills, a bunch of customization, and a sub-$30,000 price tag. The main difference is that that Runabout uses a four-cylinder gas engine, rather than electric motors. So how does it compare to Slate?

First, let's look at price. The most basic Slate you can get—cheekily called "The Blank Slate"—costs $24,950, and it's a two-door pickup with nothing more than some seats, a steering wheel, a battery, and a single rear electric motor to get you around. There's no radio, power windows, or screens to speak of.

The cheapest REO you can get will be the Runabout T4X, which costs $21,500*. Note the asterisk, as REO says the current listed price is an estimate, and the company has no factory or clear plans for getting it to market. For that shockingly low price, it's estimated that you'll get a four-cylinder engine, a choice of either a six-speed manual or automatic transmission, and mechanical four-wheel drive. It's a two-door, two-seat pickup with drop-down sides for the bed, like a Kei truck.

What four-cylinder engine will the Runabout have and which manufacturer will supply it? REO isn't saying. There are far more questions than answers so far. REO does say that it has a "targeted powertrain life of 500,000 miles." To quote myself reading that in the press release: "lol."

While Slate uses a hybrid body-on-frame style chassis, the REO has an old-school ladder frame, like a classic pickup. It's similar to slate in that it offers modular body styles, but with key differences. There's a two-door pickup and an SUV version, like Slate, but there's also a four-door pickup, which Slate doesn't have. REO claims its truck has solid rear axles, too, to give it more off-road credibility.

The design isn't bad, even if it looks like a Grand Theft Auto version of an Australian-market Land Cruiser, but that's to be expected. REO hired longtime automotive designer Frank Stephenson, whose previous work includes the first BMW-owned Mini Cooper, the Maserati MC12, and the McLaren P1. Overall, it looks handsome enough and utilitarian, even if all the photos are just renders at this point.

Inside, REO's truck is said to be pretty barebones (it hasn't been revealed yet), but not as barebones as Slate's. There's a digital screen for gauges and one for navigation, but everything else has a physical control. You're probably wondering if it has power or hand-crank windows. REO used its press release to throw a little shade: " Each model will feature power windows for convenience: hand-cranks are best left to others."

The entire idea behind REO is to offer the sort of basic pickups customers loved in the '80s and '90s, trucks that were simple utilitarian workhorses and nothing else. It's an admirable goal, especially given how expensive pickups have become. But do customers want to go backward in powertrain technology, especially with affordable mainstream electric trucks like the Ford Fathom coming to market soon?

So for less money, you can get a potentially more capable truck, in a similar configuration as the Slate, with a bit of extra interior comfort. But you lose the electric powertrain, which reduces maintenance and fuel costs. Instead, you'll have to make due with a generic four-cylinder of some sort. There is one big "if," though. You can only buy one if REO ever actually makes it. Sure, having a design by Frank Stephenson helps it feel more real, but just because they found the money to pay him to design something doesn't mean they'll actually get around to building it.

Slate is already here, it's ready to launch production vehicles soon. We've seen them in person, touched them, and tested them. Until REO can actually muster a viable product, it should probably avoid throwing anymore shade in its press releases.

Paired with a motorsport-derived all-wheel-drive system, the GR Corolla's turbocharged 1.6-liter three-cylinder is a firecracker of an engine that churns out 300 horsepower in a frenzy. A six-speed manual transmission comes standard, but a quick-shifting eight-speed automatic transmission with steering-wheel-mounted paddles is also available.

Despite its racy attitude, the GR is still a Corolla hatchback underneath. That means that its interior is comfortable, contemporary, and simply appointed, and its rear hatch lifts to expose a healthy amount of cargo space. With both fun and practicality quotients maxed out, the GR Corolla executes the hot-hatch vision expertly.

Expert Tip: The GR Corolla's primary competitors include the Honda Civic Type R and the Volkswagen Golf R. Those models are more expensive, but both the Civic and Golf beat the GR Corolla in a three-car comparison test that we conducted in 2023.

For 2026, Toyota has cooked up something special for the track rats. A GRMN Corolla joins the lineup with more aggressive bodywork, race-tuned suspension, and slightly more torque for better performance on the racetrack.

Carbon fiber bodywork—including a unique hood, an adjustable rear wing, and a unique hood—reduce weight while also providing additional downforce. The GRMN also makes use of a race-tuned suspension setup, featuring new front and rear monotube dampers with rebound springs. Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires come standard.

Other speed-focused improvements to the GRMN include a bump in torque to 302 pound-feet, a rear-seat delete, tuning adjustments to the electric power steering and the all-wheel-drive system, and a new intercooler spray system to keep the engine cool after repeated hot laps.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

Under the hood of the GR Corolla is a turbocharged three-cylinder engine plucked from Toyota's GR Yaris—a tiny hatchback that the Japanese automaker sells in global markets outside of the United States. For the GR Corolla, it has been tuned to make 300 horsepower. Buyers have the option of either a six-speed manual gearbox or eight-speed automatic with paddle shifters, and all models come with an adjustable all-wheel-drive system.

The GR-Four system allows the driver to choose among different power-distribution modes, starting with a 60/40 front-to-rear power split for everyday driving to up to 30/70 to allow for drifting antics; a 50/50 split option is intended to provide maximum traction for track driving.

Cornering grip is tenacious, and on a twisty road, the GR Corolla rewards its driver with a memorable blend of sure-footedness and civility. While pedal placement makes heel-toe downshifts difficult, the six-speed manual is otherwise easy to row; a rev-match feature is standard to smooth those downshifts. We drove the automatic version and found that it offers quick shifts and a responsive feel, plus a more relaxed demeanor when cruising on the highway. We also drove the GRMN version and were impressed with its track capabilities.

In Comparison: In a sprint to 60 mph, the 2026 GR Corolla manual we tested was quicker than the more powerful Volkswagen Golf R, which managed a 4.6-second run in our testing. Opting for the automatic will tack on an additional 0.8 second to the manual Corolla's 60 mph time.

The EPA estimates the GR Corolla's fuel economy when fitted with the six-speed manual at 21 mpg city and 28 mpg highway. Equipped with the 8-speed automatic, those numbers fall to 19 mpg city and 27 mpg highway.

On our 75-mph highway fuel economy route, a manual-transmission GR Corolla delivered 28 mpg; an automatic-equipped model returned an impressive 35 mpg. For more information about the GR Corolla's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: The GR Corolla shares most of its cabin with the standard Corolla hatchback, which means good build quality, a smattering of soft-touch materials, and plenty of features. The interior is upgraded with racier trim and sport seats. Standard equipment includes ambient interior lighting, a six-way adjustable driver's seat, push-button start, and aluminum pedal covers.

Second Row: Like the standard Corolla hatchback, space in the GR Corolla's second row is passable but not roomy. The Volkswagen Golf R provides significantly more head and legroom for rear seat passengers.

Cargo Capacity: In our testing, we were able to fit three carry-on suitcases under the GR Corolla's rear hatch with the rear seats in their upright position. With the second row folded flat, we managed to squeeze 15 carry-on bags into the cargo hold.

An 8.0-inch infotainment display with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto is standard and also includes Amazon Alexa capability and an onboard Wi-Fi hotspot. The top-tier Premium Plus trim adds a nine-speaker JBL stereo system with an Active Sound Control feature, which pumps fake engine noise into the cabin.

Toyota currently offers much of its driver-assistance technology as standard on most of its lineup, and the GR Corolla is no different. A host of desirable tech features are bundled together across the lineup and include adaptive cruise control, pedestrian and cyclist detection, and automatic high-beam headlamps.

For information about the GR Corolla's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Like other Toyotas, the GR Corolla comes with a standard warranty package enhanced by a two-year complimentary scheduled maintenance plan. All GR Corollas come with a one-year membership to the National Auto Sport Association, a sanctioning body that conducts sports car races across the U.S. The membership includes access to a complimentary high-performance driving class. If you buy a GR Corolla, take the class; you'll love it.

#4334. Waymo Has Been Banned From Operating Autonomous Vehicles on California Freeways, DMV Says

The state has put a halt on the self-driving ride-share company’s high-speed operations due to an “imminent hazard to public safety.”

The California Department of Motor Vehicles has temporarily banned autonomous rideshare operator Waymo from operating on freeways in the Golden State.

The ban went into effect on November 11, and was prompted by an “imminent hazard to public safety,” according to the California DMV. The automotive regulator said two specific incidents in which Waymo vehicles disregarded construction zones and law enforcement, pushed the ban forward, CNN reports.

The California DMV said Waymo will remain banned until it “demonstrates to the Department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.” Specifically, the Alphabet-funded autonomous vehicle operator will have to prove that its vehicles can safely detect and respond to construction zones and emergency vehicles.

The freeway restriction applies to revenue ride-share operations, as well as test vehicles. Waymo will continue to operate normally on surface streets in its California markets. Currently, Waymo operates in Los Angeles, San Diego, and the Bay Area.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state,” Waymo said in a statement to Road & Track. “In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”

One of the incidents that allegedly spurred this ban was caught on video earlier this month. The video shows California Highway Patrol patrol cars creating a traffic break on Interstate 280 near San Francisco while a Waymo vehicle attempts to pass through the rolling roadblock. California Highway Patrol officers quickly cut in front of the Waymo, which appears to stop the Waymo from attempting to pass again.

This is not the first time Waymo has faced scrutiny related to its highway operations. The company filed a recall with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration earlier this year over driving software that repeatedly entered freeway construction zones. Waymo also briefly paused highway operations in San Francisco and Los Angeles this May over similar construction zone issues, according to CNN.
